anomalies.observed: On the regulator sheet, U2 (LM1117-5.0) has its input pin VI tied to the +5V net (the same power flag that feeds C3 and the MCU VCC pins) and its output pin VO also tied to +5V. The raw input rail VCC (from J3 'PWR' pin 2, which is the only source of VCC) is not connected to the regulator at all; the regulator's IN and OUT pins are shorted together on +5V.
anomalies.expected: A 5 V linear regulator's input (VI) must be connected to the unregulated supply (VCC, the higher-voltage rail that also powers the fan through Q2/JP2), with only VO on +5V. As drawn, +5V has no source: the regulator cannot derive the logic rail from VCC.

evidence.quote: U2 LM1117-5.0 with '+5V' flag on the VI side and '+5V' flag on the VO side (right tile, row A)
J3 PWR pin 2 -> VCC (the only VCC source); U3/U4 pin 8 -> +5V (MCU supply on +5V)

anomalies.impact: The +5V logic rail is never generated, so the ATtiny and all 5V logic (pot, I2C header, reset) are unpowered; only the fan's VCC power path is energized. The controller cannot boot or regulate the fan.

parsed.summary: The LM1117-5.0 regulator U2 is mis-wired: both its input (VI) and output (VO) sit on the +5V net and the raw VCC input from J3 is not connected to it, so the 5V logic rail has no source and the MCU never powers up.
